suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the engagement clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to two material risks: first, "services" is not capitalized or defined, leaving the scope of Columbia Capital Management's obligations open to unilateral expansion or disputed interpretation by the City without objective reference to a mutually agreed description; second, the clause imposes an acceptance obligation on Columbia Capital Management with no express corresponding obligation on the City — most critically, no commitment to pay — creating an asymmetric structure under which Columbia Capital Management is contractually bound to perform without an anchored City payment duty. These deficiencies could be used to argue that Columbia Capital Management has accepted an indeterminate scope of work while the City retains discretion over its own obligations, a material financial and legal risk for Columbia Capital Management in any fee or scope dispute.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 1. Engagement. The City hereby engages Consultant as an independent contractor to perform the services described in this Agreement and Consultant accepts that engagement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 1. Engagement. The City hereby engages Consultant as an independent contractor to perform the Services described in this Agreement, and in consideration thereof the City shall compensate Consultant in accordance with this Agreement. Consultant accepts such engagement.

suggestions.reason: Because the clause does not define what falls outside the Contract Services, the City could assert that ancillary investment-related activities—such as reporting, compliance monitoring, or advisory work—are implicitly captured within the broad "Investment Management Services" description in Exhibit A, exposing Columbia Capital Management to scope creep without additional compensation. The absence of an express exclusion of out-of-scope services creates a gap that undermines the written amendment mechanism that is otherwise the only protection Columbia Capital Management has against uncompensated additional work. Without a clear boundary, Columbia Capital Management bears the burden of disputing scope in real time rather than relying on a defined contractual limit, which is a material operational and financial risk. Counsel should also confirm that Exhibit A sets out services with sufficient specificity to allow an independent determination of performance, rather than relying solely on a broad category heading.
suggestions.original_text: Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform those services (“Contract Services”) described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement and incorporated herein by reference. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement. At the City’s request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of the additional work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, except on the basis of the provisions of a written supplemental agreement or an amendment signed by the Parties.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform those services ("Contract Services") described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement and incorporated herein by reference. Any services not expressly described in Exhibit A are outside the scope of the Contract Services and do not constitute obligations of Consultant under this Agreement. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement. At the City's request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of the additional work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, except on the basis of the provisions of a written supplemental agreement or an amendment signed by the Parties.

suggestions.reason: Section 3 as drafted contains no operative payment mechanics whatsoever — it merely incorporates Exhibit A by reference without stating how fees are calculated, when the Consultant may invoice, when the City must pay, or what happens if payment is late. For Columbia Capital Management, acting as the Consultant, this creates serious financial exposure: without an agreed invoicing cadence, payment deadline, or late-payment remedy, the City retains de facto discretion over when — or whether — to pay, leaving Columbia Capital Management without an enforceable collection mechanism. The absence of any invoice dispute procedure also means the City could withhold the entire invoice amount on a minor objection, further impairing Columbia Capital Management's cash position. The clause should also address whether expenses are recoverable, as silent treatment defaults to exclusion and would leave Columbia Capital Management bearing out-of-pocket costs without recourse.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 3. Compensation and Expenses. As set forth in Exhibit A, the City shall pay the Consultant for the Contract Services it performs as outlined in Section 2 of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the City may terminate this Agreement for cause—potentially triggering reputational harm, disputed payment entitlements, or indemnity exposure—without affording Columbia Capital Management any opportunity to cure an alleged breach before termination takes effect. The absence of a cure period is materially prejudicial to Columbia Capital Management because it allows the City to escalate from alleged breach to termination without prior notice specifying the deficiency, eliminating any practical remedy for Columbia Capital Management. Additionally, the clause conflates termination for convenience and termination for cause into a single notice framework without distinguishing the substantive grounds for a cause-based termination, leaving "cause" undefined and susceptible to overreach by the City. Clarifying that cause-based termination requires both specification of the material breach and a reasonable cure period protects Columbia Capital Management's right to continue performing and receiving compensation under the Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 4. Termination of Agreement. The City may terminate this Agreement at any time on and after November 30, 2024, with sixty (60) days’ written notice for convenience or cause upon written notice to Consultant. If the City terminates the Agreement under this Section, the City shall pay the Consultant for Contract Services satisfactorily performed by Consultant before the termination, and for all associated expenses incurred by the Consultant before the termination. Under no circumstances will the Consultant be entitled to anticipatory profits or consequential damages. Consultant may terminate the agreement at any time upon sixty (60) days’ written notice. The provisions regarding indemnity and insurance shall survive the termination of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 4. Termination of Agreement. The City may terminate this Agreement at any time on and after November 30, 2024, for convenience upon sixty (60) days' written notice to Consultant, such termination to be effective upon expiration of the notice period. The City may terminate this Agreement for cause only upon written notice to Consultant specifying the nature of the material breach in reasonable detail, provided that Consultant has failed to cure such breach within thirty (30) days following receipt of such notice. If the City terminates the Agreement under this Section, the City shall pay the Consultant for Contract Services satisfactorily performed by Consultant before the termination, and for all associated expenses incurred by the Consultant before the termination. Under no circumstances will the Consultant be entitled to anticipatory profits or consequential damages. Consultant may terminate the agreement at any time upon sixty (60) days' written notice. The provisions regarding indemnity and insurance shall survive the termination of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the compliance obligation imposes no duty on the Consultant to notify Columbia Capital Management of a breach affecting performance, is silent on who bears the cost of compliance with changes in law following execution, and omits any reference to anti-bribery, anti-corruption, or labor standards obligations addressing forced labor and human trafficking. These gaps expose Columbia Capital Management to unquantified financial and reputational risk: a Consultant who discovers a legal violation can remain silent, cost increases from regulatory change may be redirected to Columbia Capital Management, and the absence of ethics and labor-standards standards weakens Columbia Capital Management's supply-chain governance position. The indemnification in the second sentence does not cure these gaps because it is reactive rather than preventive, and there is no mechanism to trigger the indemnity until harm has already occurred.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 6. Compliance with Laws. Consultant shall comply with local, state, and federal rules, regulations, and laws pertaining to this Agreement that are applicable at the time the Consultant conducts the Contract Services, regardless of whether such requirements are specifically referred to in this Agreement. Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents against any claim or liability arising from or based on any violation of the same.

suggestions.clause: Compliance with Equal Opportunity Laws, Regulations, and Rules
suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted limits Consultant's compliance obligations to two Kansas-specific anti-discrimination statutes, leaving Columbia Capital Management exposed because it contains no obligation to comply with applicable anti-bribery and corruption laws, no prohibition on forced labor or human trafficking in Consultant's supply chain, and no requirement for Consultant to notify Columbia Capital Management if a legal breach affecting the Agreement occurs. If Consultant engages in corrupt conduct or uses a supply chain involving exploitative labor practices, Columbia Capital Management would have no express contractual basis to treat such conduct as a breach or to claim immediate remediation. The absence of a breach-notification obligation further means Columbia Capital Management could remain unaware of regulatory violations affecting the Agreement's performance until significant damage has occurred.
suggestions.original_text: Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant agrees to comply with the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.) and the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.) and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant agrees to comply with the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.) and the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.) and all other applicable laws and regulations, including those relating to anti-bribery, corruption, and the prohibition of forced labor and human trafficking, and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age. Consultant shall promptly notify Columbia Capital Management in writing of any breach of applicable law that affects the performance of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The insurance obligation currently runs only "throughout the duration of this Agreement," leaving Columbia Capital Management exposed after expiration or termination to claims arising from services performed during the term, particularly professional liability claims that frequently emerge well after project completion. Without a post-termination tail period, the Consultant could allow coverage to lapse the moment the Agreement ends, eliminating any practical recovery path for Columbia Capital Management on latent errors or omissions. Additionally, the clause contains no express statement that the insurance procured does not cap or satisfy the Consultant's underlying liability, which creates a risk that the Consultant will argue its obligation to Columbia Capital Management is effectively capped at policy limits, undermining the full scope of remedies available under the Agreement.
suggestions.original_text: General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The City shall be named as  an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers’ compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement’s execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.
suggestions.suggested_fix: General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement and for a period of not less than two (2) years following its expiration or termination, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The procurement of insurance required under this Agreement shall not be construed to limit or satisfy Consultant's liability to the City. The City shall be named as an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers' compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement's execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 9 imposes a broad, one-sided indemnification obligation exclusively on Columbia Capital Management, with no reciprocal protection from the City for claims arising out of the City's own negligent or intentional acts—exposing Columbia Capital Management to liability for losses it did not cause. The requirement to give "immediate" written notice places an unreasonably strict trigger on Columbia Capital Management, while the clause is entirely silent on Columbia Capital Management's right to control the defense, approve settlements, and require the City's cooperation, leaving Columbia Capital Management financially exposed to adverse outcomes in litigation it cannot direct. The absence of any mitigation obligation on the City means the City has no contractual duty to limit recoverable losses, further increasing Columbia Capital Management's indemnity exposure. Additionally, the prefatory language "without in any way limiting indemnification obligations that may be set forth elsewhere in this Agreement" creates additive, uncapped exposure across the Agreement with no stated relationship to any liability limitations.
suggestions.original_text: Section 9. Indemnification. Without in any way limiting indemnification obligations that may be set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the  City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys’ fees, arising out of or resulting from the performance of Consultant’s services, provided that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Consultant, its subcontractors, anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them, or anyone for whose acts any of them may be liable, whether or not arising before or after completion of Consultant’s services. Consultant shall give the City immediate written notice of any claim, suit, or demand that may be subject to this provision.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 9. Indemnification. Without in any way limiting indemnification obligations that may be set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys' fees, arising out of or resulting from the performance of Consultant's services, to the extent that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Consultant, its subcontractors, anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them, or anyone for whose acts any of them may be liable. The City shall, to the same extent, defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Consultant and its officers, employees, and agents from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys' fees, caused by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the City or its agents. The party seeking indemnification shall give the other party prompt written notice of any claim, suit, or demand that may be subject to this provision, shall take reasonable steps to mitigate its losses, and shall cooperate reasonably in the defense of such claim. The indemnifying party shall have the right to control the defense and shall not be bound by any settlement made without its prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.

suggestions.reason: The clause creates two discrete risks for Columbia Capital Management as the Consultant. First, the phrase "third party beneficiary relationship" is undefined and unqualified, leaving open whether it covers only express beneficiary arrangements or also implied ones; this ambiguity could allow a creative claimant to argue that the clause does not bar an implied third-party claim against Columbia Capital Management. Second, and more materially, the residual carve-out that duties "shall remain as imposed by law" is unanchored: it does not specify applicable law, leaving Columbia Capital Management potentially exposed to an indeterminate body of statutory, regulatory, or common-law duties whose scope a court would have to determine through extrinsic evidence. Anchoring the residual duties to "applicable law" and confining them to those "expressly" imposed closes both ambiguities without altering the commercial substance of the clause.
suggestions.original_text: Section 10. No Third Party Beneficiaries. City and Consultant specifically agree that this Agreement is not intended to create any third party beneficiary relationship nor to authorize anyone not a party to this Agreement to maintain a suit for personal injuries or property damage pursuant to the terms or provisions of this Agreement; the duties, obligations and responsibilities of the parties to this Agreement with respect to third parties shall remain as imposed by law.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 10. No Third Party Beneficiaries. City and Consultant specifically agree that this Agreement is not intended to create any third party beneficiary relationship, whether express or implied, nor to authorize anyone not a party to this Agreement to maintain a suit for personal injuries or property damage pursuant to the terms or provisions of this Agreement; the duties, obligations and responsibilities of the parties to this Agreement with respect to third parties shall remain only as expressly imposed by applicable law.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 11 leaves Columbia Capital Management, as Consultant, exposed to material legal and financial risk on multiple fronts: there is no governing law, no identified forum, and the "take such steps as it deems necessary" language gives either claiming party unconstrained latitude to initiate proceedings in any venue at any time, without any objective timeframe governing the negotiation phase. Most critically, the obligation to continue performing "as though no dispute exists" falls solely and unconditionally on Columbia Capital Management, with no reciprocal obligation on the City to continue making payments during the dispute period — meaning Columbia Capital Management could be compelled to keep performing under a contract where the City has stopped paying, with no recourse short of termination. The absence of a governing law and forum designation also creates enforcement uncertainty that could significantly complicate any recovery action by Columbia Capital Management.
suggestions.original_text: Section 11. Disputes. The City and Consultant agree that disputes relative to the Contract Services of this Agreement should first be addressed by negotiations between the parties. If direct negotiations fail to resolve the dispute, the party initiating the claim that is the basis of the dispute shall be free to take such steps as it deems necessary to protect its interest; provided, however, that notwithstanding any such dispute, the Consultant shall proceed with its services under this Agreement as though no dispute exists.

suggestions.reason: As drafted, this clause contains nothing more than an anti-collusion pricing warranty, leaving Columbia Capital Management entirely unprotected on the substance of what it is actually procuring. Without an express standard of performance, a law-compliance warranty, and a non-infringement warranty, Columbia Capital Management has no contractual basis to demand re-performance or a refund if the Services are deficient, unlawful, or infringe a third party's intellectual property rights. This exposure is material: Columbia Capital Management could face regulatory liability, third-party IP claims, or substandard deliverables with no warranty remedy to enforce against the counterparty.
suggestions.original_text: The price submitted and the costs comprising same are independently arrived at without collusion.
suggestions.suggested_fix: The price submitted and the costs comprising same are independently arrived at without collusion. The Services shall be performed with reasonable skill and care, in compliance with applicable laws, and without infringement of any third party's intellectual property rights. In the event of a breach of the foregoing warranties, the breaching party shall, at Columbia Capital Management's election, re-perform the affected Services at no additional cost or refund the fees paid therefor.

suggestions.reason: The authority representation runs exclusively from Consultant, leaving no corresponding warranty that Columbia Capital Management itself has the requisite power and authority to execute and perform the Agreement. This gap creates a material enforceability risk for Columbia Capital Management: if a dispute arises, Consultant could challenge the binding effect of the Agreement on the basis that Columbia Capital Management never warranted its own authority to enter into it. Market-standard professional services agreements require mutual authority representations from both contracting parties to establish a fully enforceable contractual relationship.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Each party has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The warranty standards in this clause — "recognized professional standards prevalent in their field," "state of the art procedures and techniques," and "ready comprehension of the required subject matter" — are undefined and subjective, meaning that if the Consultant delivers deficient work, it can dispute what those standards require, leaving Columbia Capital Management with an unenforceable warranty in practice. The phrase "state of the art" is particularly problematic, as it is both aspirational and contested, allowing the Consultant to argue that any reasonable level of competence satisfies the standard regardless of actual performance quality. Critically, the clause imposes a warranty obligation on the Consultant but provides Columbia Capital Management with no express remedy upon breach, such as a right to require re-performance at no additional cost, which undermines the practical value of the warranty entirely. Anchoring the standards to objectively determinable measures and adding a corresponding remedy right for Columbia Capital Management corrects both the enforceability gap and the one-sided structure.
suggestions.original_text: Section 13. Quality Assurance. Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement, shall conform to or exceed the recognized professional standards prevalent in their field. Further, the Consultant warrants that all work and service performed under this Agreement shall be performed with the professional expertise, skills, and knowledge of state of the art procedures and techniques in all relevant subject matters. The Consultant accordingly shall be capable of performing the necessary consulting and other services required herein and possess the ready comprehension of the required subject matter and the expertise to provide these services.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 13. Quality Assurance. Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement shall conform to or exceed generally accepted professional standards applicable to the relevant field. Further, the Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement shall be performed with the professional expertise, skills, and knowledge of industry-standard procedures and techniques in all relevant subject matters. The Consultant accordingly shall be capable of performing the necessary consulting and other services required herein and possess sufficient comprehension of the required subject matter and the expertise to provide these services. In the event of a breach of the foregoing warranties, Consultant shall re-perform the non-conforming work or services promptly and at no additional cost to Columbia Capital Management.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 14 imposes an assignment restriction solely on Consultant, meaning the City retains an unrestricted right to assign the Agreement to any successor or transferee without Columbia Capital Management's knowledge or approval — exposing Columbia Capital Management to the risk of being bound to perform for a counterparty it did not select and may not have agreed to serve. The City's consent right carries no reasonableness standard, no deemed-approval mechanism, and no response deadline, giving the City unfettered discretion to block legitimate corporate transactions by Columbia Capital Management, including internal reorganizations or transfers to affiliates. The existing successor-binding language applies only to Consultant's assigns with no reciprocal obligation on the City's successors, leaving Columbia Capital Management without recourse if the City undergoes a change of control or is succeeded by an entity with materially different characteristics. There is also no continuing liability obligation on the assigning party and no notice requirement for any transfer, leaving Columbia Capital Management with no protection against a de facto substitution of counterparty.
suggestions.original_text: Section 14. Assignment. Neither this Agreement nor any rights or obligations hereunder shall be assigned or otherwise transferred by Consultant without the prior written consent of the City. This Agreement is binding upon and fully enforceable against the successors and assigns of Consultant, whether consented to or not.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 14. Assignment. Neither this Agreement nor any rights or obligations hereunder shall be assigned or otherwise transferred by either party without the prior written consent of the other party, not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed, and deemed given if no written objection is delivered within fifteen (15) days of written request; provided that Consultant may assign this Agreement to an affiliate or to a successor entity in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets upon written notice to the City. Any permitted assignee shall assume all obligations hereunder in writing, and the assigning party shall remain liable for performance of all obligations accrued prior to such assignment. Either party may terminate this Agreement upon written notice if the other party undergoes a change of control resulting in assignment to a direct competitor. This Agreement is binding upon and fully enforceable against the permitted successors and assigns of each party.

suggestions.reason: The notices clause sets out Columbia Capital Management's address details but contains no mechanism for either party to update those details over time. Without such a provision, Columbia Capital Management has no clear contractual basis to change its designated contact or address if its Compliance Officer, suite location, or other details change during the term, creating a risk that notices sent to an outdated address could be deemed validly delivered against Columbia Capital Management. This gap equally affects Columbia Capital Management's ability to rely on counterparty contact details if the other party relocates or changes its representative without formal notice.
suggestions.original_text: Columbia Capital Management, LLC Attn: Compliance Officer 6700 Antioch Rd., Suite 250 Merriam, KS 66204
suggestions.suggested_fix: Columbia Capital Management, LLC Attn: Compliance Officer 6700 Antioch Rd., Suite 250 Merriam, KS 66204. Either party may update its notice details by providing written notice of the change to the other party, such change to be effective ten (10) days following receipt of that written notice.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 16 omits three protections that are material to Columbia Capital Management's interests as Consultant. First, the clause is silent on who controls the manner and means of performance, which is a foundational element of independent contractor status; without it, the City could later argue operational control over Columbia Capital Management's personnel, undermining that status and exposing Columbia Capital Management to reclassification risk. Second, the clause imposes tax and withholding obligations solely on Columbia Capital Management without establishing that the City bears equivalent responsibility for the costs, benefits, and employment taxes of its own personnel, creating an asymmetric allocation that could be used against Columbia Capital Management if the relationship is ever scrutinized by a taxing authority. Third, the absence of a mutual no-authority-to-bind provision means there is no express contractual barrier to the City acting as though it has agency authority over Columbia Capital Management, which could expose Columbia Capital Management to unauthorized commitments made by City personnel.
suggestions.original_text: Section 16. Independent Contractor. In no event, while performing under this Agreement, shall Consultant be deemed to be acting as an employee of the City; rather, Consultant shall be deemed to be an independent contractor. Consultant shall be responsible for and pay all taxes and withholdings required by law upon the compensation paid under this Agreement, and shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City from liability in connection therewith. Nothing expressed herein or implied herein shall be construed as creating between Consultant and the City the relationships of employer and employee, principal and agent, a partnership, or a joint venture.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 16. Independent Contractor. In no event, while performing under this Agreement, shall Consultant be deemed to be acting as an employee of the City; rather, Consultant shall be deemed to be an independent contractor who retains sole control over the manner and means of performing the Services. Neither party shall have authority to bind or obligate the other party to any third party or commitment. Consultant shall be responsible for and pay all taxes and withholdings required by law upon the compensation paid under this Agreement, and shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City from liability in connection therewith. Each party shall be solely responsible for all compensation, benefits, and employment-related costs of its own respective personnel. Nothing expressed herein or implied herein shall be construed as creating between Consultant and the City the relationships of employer and employee, principal and agent, a partnership, or a joint venture.

suggestions.clause: Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law
suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 17 addresses only the City's budget appropriation constraints and contains no anti-bribery or corruption compliance obligation, no requirement for either party to notify the other of a law breach affecting the Agreement, and no supply-chain due-diligence standard — leaving Columbia Capital Management exposed to reputational and regulatory risk if it continues performing services under a contract where the counterparty is engaged in corrupt conduct or where a material legal breach goes unreported. The absence of a breach-notification obligation is particularly prejudicial to Columbia Capital Management because it may continue expending resources and foregoing other opportunities with no warning that a legal impediment has arisen that could prevent payment. The addition of a mutual compliance and notification obligation, together with an anti-bribery and supply-chain standard, is a market-standard requirement that also supports Columbia Capital Management's own regulatory compliance posture under applicable professional and financial-services frameworks.
suggestions.original_text: Section 17. Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law. This Agreement must comply with the applicable provisions of the Kansas Cash-Basis Law, K.S.A. 10-1101 et seq., as amended. The City is obligated only to pay periodic payments or monthly installments under this Agreement as may lawfully be made from funds budgeted and appropriated for the purposes set forth in this Agreement during the City’s current budget year. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the event that the City does not budget and appropriate funds for any renewal term, for any reason in its sole discretion, the parties agree that they shall be relieved of all obligations under this Agreement without penalty. To the extent that the City does budget and appropriate funds for the purposes set forth in this Agreement, the obligations of the parties shall remain as provided herein.

suggestions.reason: The venue clause designates the District Court of Johnson County, Kansas as the "sole and exclusive" forum but is silent on federal court, creating operative ambiguity that could expose Columbia Capital Management to procedural disputes. Where a claim arising out of this Agreement falls within federal subject matter jurisdiction — for example, by reason of diversity of citizenship or a federal statutory cause of action — a court could read this clause either as precluding federal court entirely (potentially waiving rights Columbia Capital Management may need to enforce) or as inapplicable to such claims, leaving venue unresolved and subject to litigation. That uncertainty undermines the certainty the exclusivity language was intended to provide, and could force Columbia Capital Management into protracted threshold disputes before the merits of any claim are addressed.
suggestions.original_text: Section 18. Legal Action. The parties agree that the sole and exclusive venue for any legal actions arising out of this Agreement shall be the District Court of Johnson County, Kansas.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 18. Legal Action. The parties agree that the sole and exclusive venue for any legal actions arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be the District Court of Johnson County, Kansas, or, to the extent federal jurisdiction applies, the United States District Court for the District of Kansas, and each party hereby irrevocably submits to the personal jurisdiction of such courts for such purpose.

suggestions.reason: The current clause does nothing more than designate Kansas law as the governing law; it is silent on venue, forum, pre-dispute escalation, continuation of performance, and the right to seek emergency relief. For Columbia Capital Management, this creates serious practical exposure: a counterparty could file suit in any jurisdiction it selects, forcing Columbia Capital Management to litigate in an inconvenient or hostile forum, with no obligation to negotiate before triggering costly formal proceedings and no requirement to continue performing during a dispute. The absence of these elements also means Columbia Capital Management has no contractual basis to seek urgent injunctive relief without arguably waiving its dispute-resolution rights, and cross-references to any termination-for-breach provisions are further undermined because performance obligations during a dispute remain undefined.
suggestions.original_text: Section 19. Governing Law. This Agreement, the rights and obligations of the parties, and any claim or dispute arising hereunder shall be construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Kansas.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "automatically be considered reformed and amended so as to conform to all applicable legal requirements" is operationally ambiguous: it does not identify who performs the reformation, by what substantive standard, or what the reformed provision must achieve — leaving open the possibility that a counterparty could contend that an invalid provision has been unilaterally "auto-reformed" in a manner adverse to Columbia Capital Management without Columbia Capital Management's participation or consent. Because the mechanism is self-described as automatic, a court could not give it precise operative effect without resort to extrinsic evidence about what the parties intended the reformed provision to say. For Columbia Capital Management, this creates a concrete risk that a commercially material provision is rewritten in a way that departs from the agreed economic or risk-allocation bargain, with no structured process to ensure Columbia Capital Management's interests are reflected in the replacement language.
suggestions.original_text: Section 22. Invalidity. If any provision in this Agreement shall be adjudicated invalid under applicable laws, such invalid provision shall automatically be considered reformed and amended so as to conform to all applicable legal requirements, or, if such invalidity cannot be cured by reformation or amendment, the same shall be considered stricken and deleted, but in neither such event or events shall the validity or enforceability of the remaining valid portions hereof be affected thereby.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 22. Invalidity. If any provision in this Agreement shall be adjudicated invalid under applicable laws, the parties shall replace such invalid provision with a valid provision that most closely approximates the original intent and economic effect of the invalid provision, or, if such invalidity cannot be cured by such replacement, the same shall be considered stricken and deleted, but in neither such event or events shall the validity or enforceability of the remaining valid portions hereof be affected thereby.

suggestions.reason: The current waiver clause protects both parties against implied waivers arising from inaction and requires written, signed waivers, but it omits the standard principle that a waiver of one specific breach or right does not operate as a waiver of any other or future breach or right. Without this language, a counterparty could argue that a written waiver granted by Columbia Capital Management in one instance — for example, overlooking a missed deliverable deadline — constitutes a broader or precedential waiver of Columbia Capital Management's rights in respect of related or subsequent breaches. This gap materially undermines Columbia Capital Management's ability to enforce its contractual rights on a selective, instance-specific basis without that enforcement being challenged by reference to any prior waiver it has extended.
suggestions.original_text: Section 23. Waiver. The failure of either party to insist upon the strict performance of any of the terms or conditions of this Agreement or to exercise any option, right, or remedy herein contained, shall not be construed as a waiver or relinquishment for the future of such term, provision, option, right, or remedy, but the same shall continue and remain in full force and effect. No waiver by either party of any term or provision hereof shall be deemed to have been made unless expressed in writing and signed by the waiving party.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 23. Waiver. The failure of either party to insist upon the strict performance of any of the terms or conditions of this Agreement or to exercise any option, right, or remedy herein contained, shall not be construed as a waiver or relinquishment for the future of such term, provision, option, right, or remedy, but the same shall continue and remain in full force and effect. No waiver by either party of any term or provision hereof shall be deemed to have been made unless expressed in writing and signed by the waiving party. No waiver of any breach or right under this Agreement shall constitute or be deemed a waiver of any other or subsequent breach or right, whether of the same or of a different nature.

suggestions.reason: The current clause exposes Columbia Capital Management to three related risks: first, by requiring only the signature of "both parties" without specifying authorized representatives, it creates a risk that an amendment could be argued to have been signed by a person lacking authority, potentially binding Columbia Capital Management to terms it did not sanction at the appropriate level; second, the clause is silent on whether schedules and exhibits are covered, leaving open an argument that attached commercial terms—such as pricing schedules or service orders—could be varied informally outside this provision; third, the absence of any anti-waiver or anti-oral-modification language means that a course of conduct or verbal agreement by Columbia Capital Management's personnel could be asserted to modify material obligations under the Agreement, a risk that is particularly acute in an ongoing professional services relationship where day-to-day interactions are frequent.
suggestions.original_text: Section 26. Amendments. This Agreement may not be amended unless such amendment is in writing and signed by both parties.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 26. Amendments. This Agreement, including all schedules and exhibits hereto, may not be amended unless such amendment is in writing and signed by an authorized representative of each party. No oral agreement, course of conduct, or course of dealing shall constitute or be deemed an amendment to this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, Section 27 expressly identifies only the Consultant's obligations as surviving termination, leaving Columbia Capital Management without an express post-termination right to enforce corresponding protections — such as the right to call upon the Consultant's indemnification and insurance coverage after the Agreement ends. The catch-all phrase "any other terms and conditions that by their nature should survive termination" is sufficiently vague that a court could reach different conclusions about which provisions it captures, creating litigation risk for Columbia Capital Management if it seeks to enforce confidentiality, intellectual property, or payment obligations after termination. The combination of the one-sided enumeration and the ambiguous catch-all means that Columbia Capital Management's post-termination rights rest on an uncertain legal foundation, while the Consultant could argue that obligations imposed on it beyond Sections 8 and 9 have expired. Replacing "by their nature should survive" with "by their express terms or nature are intended to survive" and re-anchoring the clause to both parties eliminates the asymmetry and reduces interpretive uncertainty.
suggestions.original_text: Section 27. Survivorship. Notwithstanding the termination of this Agreement, Consultant’s obligations with respect to Insurance (Section 8) and Indemnification (Section 9), and any other terms and conditions that by their nature should survive termination, shall survive the termination of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 27. Survivorship. Notwithstanding the termination of this Agreement, each party's rights and obligations with respect to Insurance (Section 8) and Indemnification (Section 9), and any other provisions that by their express terms or nature are intended to survive termination, shall survive the termination of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking" imposes an open-ended, undefined compliance obligation on Columbia Capital Management with no discernible boundaries — any law, regulation, or rule that a court might conceivably characterize as "applicable" could be invoked to establish a breach, creating effectively uncapped liability exposure for Columbia Capital Management with no corresponding obligation imposed on the City in this clause. The absence of any City-side obligation — such as a duty to provide accurate account information or reasonable cooperation — leaves Columbia Capital Management contractually bound to manage the Accounts without the City being required to furnish the data and access necessary for Consultant to perform. Replacing the vague legal compliance standard with a scoped reference to applicable federal, state, and local laws governing investment advisory services, and adding a reciprocal City cooperation obligation, addresses both the indefiniteness risk and the one-sided structure of this appointment clause.
suggestions.original_text: Appointment of Consultant. The City hereby appoints Consultant to act as the investment adviser and to assume the responsibilities of investment management of the pooled cash of the City including all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts and bond proceeds (the “Accounts”). Consultant does hereby accept said appointment as an investment adviser under the Accounts. By accepting such appointment, Consultant agrees that at all times it shall act in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Appointment of Consultant. The City hereby appoints Consultant to act as the investment adviser and to assume the responsibilities of investment management of the pooled cash of the City including all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts and bond proceeds (the "Accounts"). Consultant does hereby accept said appointment as an investment adviser under the Accounts. By accepting such appointment, Consultant agrees that at all times it shall act in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations governing investment advisory services. The City shall provide Consultant with all information and cooperation reasonably necessary to enable Consultant to perform its obligations under this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The prudent-person standard as drafted relies on the phrase "an enterprise of like character and with like aims," which is undefined anywhere in the Agreement and has no objective anchor, leaving its meaning entirely open to dispute. If a performance dispute arises, Consultant could argue that the applicable benchmark is a less rigorous comparator, effectively diluting the fiduciary duty Columbia Capital Management bargained for and weakening its ability to hold Consultant accountable for underperformance or mismanagement of assets. Additionally, the standard as written offers Columbia Capital Management no enforceable, objectively determinable benchmark a court could apply without resort to extrinsic evidence, increasing litigation risk and unpredictability. Anchoring the standard to a professional investment adviser managing comparable assets for institutional clients removes the ambiguity and aligns the clause with the actual nature of the engagement.
suggestions.original_text: Fiduciary. In addition to, but not in lieu of any and all applicable fiduciary standards imposed under federal or state law, Consultant shall act as a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement. As a fiduciary, Consultant shall perform its duties under this Agreement with the care, skill, prudence, and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent person acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in an enterprise of like character and with like aims.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Fiduciary. In addition to, but not in lieu of any and all applicable fiduciary standards imposed under federal or state law, Consultant shall act as a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement. As a fiduciary, Consultant shall perform its duties under this Agreement with the care, skill, prudence, and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent professional investment adviser acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use when managing comparable assets for institutional clients.

suggestions.reason: The obligation to provide "periodic portfolio reporting" leaves the reporting frequency entirely undefined, exposing Columbia Capital Management to disputed claims of breach if the City asserts that reporting was insufficient without any objective standard against which to measure compliance. The absence of a defined interval also means the City could demand reporting on any frequency it chooses, creating an open-ended and potentially burdensome obligation for Columbia Capital Management with no contractual ceiling. Additionally, without specifying the form or format in which the required information is to be delivered, two reasonable parties could interpret the scope of the obligation differently, leaving Columbia Capital Management vulnerable to claims that its reporting did not satisfy this provision.
suggestions.original_text: Providing periodic portfolio reporting to the City, including information on holdings, transactions, portfolio income and performance.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Providing monthly portfolio reporting to the City, including information on holdings, transactions, portfolio income and performance, in a form mutually agreed upon by the parties in writing.

suggestions.reason: The clause assigns full responsibility for investment and management to Columbia Capital Management without qualification, while simultaneously permitting the City to issue new or amended investment policy objectives and guidelines at any time, without any notice requirement. This "from time to time" mechanism creates direct exposure for Columbia Capital Management: the City could unilaterally modify the governing guidelines after a transaction has been executed, leaving Columbia Capital Management liable for decisions that were fully consistent with the guidelines in effect at the time of execution. Additionally, the undefined interplay between "sole discretion" and the City's open-ended guideline-amendment right effectively negates the discretion granted, without any corresponding protection for Columbia Capital Management where it acts in good faith on the last received written guidelines. These combined deficiencies mean that the responsibility assignment in the second sentence could be construed as imposing strict liability on Columbia Capital Management irrespective of whether it had the information necessary to comply.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant shall invest and otherwise manage the assets held by the City, its banks and any Custodian in the Accounts. Responsibility for the investment and management is assigned to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have sole discretion with respect to investment of funds in the Accounts without prior consultation with the City; however, Consultant shall be bound by such written investment policy objectives and guidelines for the management of the assets as shall from time to time be provided to Consultant by the City. Consultant shall have the authority to select the brokerage firms, consistent with the requirements of K.S.A. 12-1675(b)(4), through which orders will be placed. Consultant may combine orders for the Accounts with orders for other accounts or funds under management. Consultant shall effect all purchases and sales of securities in a manner consistent with the principles of best execution, taking into account net price (including commissions) and execution capability and other services that the broker or dealer may provide. Consultant shall use investment strategies designed to ensure that all securities transactions are executed in such a manner that the total explicit and implicit costs and total proceeds in every transaction are the most favorable under the circumstances. Consultant shall issue suitable instructions to the Custodian with respect to deliveries and payments.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Consultant shall invest and otherwise manage the assets held by the City, its banks and any Custodian in the Accounts. Responsibility for the investment and management is assigned to Consultant by the City, subject to Consultant's right to rely on the most recently received written investment policy objectives and guidelines until any updated guidelines become effective in accordance with this clause. Consultant shall have sole discretion with respect to investment of funds in the Accounts without prior consultation with the City; however, Consultant shall be bound by such written investment policy objectives and guidelines for the management of the assets as shall from time to time be provided to Consultant by the City, provided that any new or amended investment policy objectives and guidelines shall be delivered to Consultant in writing not less than ten (10) Business Days prior to the date on which Consultant is required to act in accordance therewith, and Consultant shall not be liable for investment decisions made in reasonable reliance on the most recently received written guidelines prior to receipt and effectiveness of any updated guidelines. Consultant shall have the authority to select the brokerage firms, consistent with the requirements of K.S.A. 12-1675(b)(4), through which orders will be placed. Consultant may combine orders for the Accounts with orders for other accounts or funds under management. Consultant shall effect all purchases and sales of securities in a manner consistent with the principles of best execution, taking into account net price (including commissions) and execution capability and other services that the broker or dealer may provide. Consultant shall use investment strategies designed to ensure that all securities transactions are executed in such a manner that the total explicit and implicit costs and total proceeds in every transaction are the most favorable under the circumstances. Consultant shall issue suitable instructions to the Custodian with respect to deliveries and payments.

suggestions.reason: The obligation to "Timely provide" account balances, statements, and interest data is unenforceable as written because "timely" is an undefined standard that two reasonable lawyers would read differently, leaving Columbia Capital Management with no objective trigger to compel the City's compliance. As the investment Consultant, Columbia Capital Management depends on accurate and current account data to execute the investment plan; if the City delays indefinitely, Columbia Capital Management bears the operational and reputational risk of portfolio decisions made on stale information, yet has no contractual basis to establish breach. Anchoring the obligation to a specific calendar period eliminates this ambiguity and gives Columbia Capital Management a measurable, enforceable right.
suggestions.original_text: Timely provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City’s funds and accounts.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Within five (5) Business Days following the close of each calendar month, provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City's funds and accounts.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the City's obligation to supply historical account balances and monthly account cash flows is triggered solely "upon request" by the Consultant, meaning the City bears no proactive duty to deliver information that is foundational to Columbia Capital Management's ability to determine required liquidity and execute the investment mandate. This entirely reactive structure exposes Columbia Capital Management to material performance risk: if the City delays responding to or disregards a request, Columbia Capital Management may be left making investment decisions on stale or incomplete data, yet remain contractually responsible for the quality of those decisions. The absence of any timing standard for the City's compliance further compounds this risk, as there is no mechanism to compel timely delivery. To protect Columbia Capital Management's operational effectiveness, the provision should impose a proactive periodic delivery obligation rather than a purely request-triggered one.
suggestions.original_text: Upon request, provide Consultant with historical account balances and monthly account cash flows to permit Consultant to properly determine required liquidity.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Provide Consultant with historical account balances and monthly account cash flows on a monthly basis, and upon Consultant's request within a reasonable period of such request, to permit Consultant to properly determine required liquidity.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "the investment plan" is undefined in this clause and, as indicated, lacks a definition elsewhere in the Agreement, creating a material risk for Columbia Capital Management. Because the City's obligation to execute wire transfers is conditioned on the request being "necessary to effect the investment plan," an undefined plan allows the City to dispute whether any particular transfer request falls within scope, effectively enabling the City to block or delay Columbia Capital Management's investment execution. In an investment management context, delays caused by disputed transfer requests can result in missed market opportunities and direct financial harm to Columbia Capital Management's performance obligations. Anchoring the obligation to a written investment plan prepared and maintained by Columbia Capital Management removes that ambiguity and prevents the City from using a definitional gap to resist legitimate transfer instructions.
suggestions.original_text: Upon request and with reasonable notice, respond to Consultant’s requests to move money via Federal Reserve wire or other means between the City’s various accounts as necessary to effect the investment plan.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Upon request and with reasonable notice, respond to Consultant's requests to move money via Federal Reserve wire or other means between the City's various accounts as necessary to effect the written investment plan prepared and maintained by Consultant.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the clause imposes no timeframe within which the City must instruct the Custodian after receiving confirmations from Consultant, exposing Columbia Capital Management to settlement failure, market risk, and potential regulatory breach if the City delays acting on trade confirmations. The term "copies of confirmations" is undefined, creating a dispute risk as to whether Columbia Capital Management has discharged its notification obligation and what document format or delivery method satisfies the condition precedent to the City's instruction duty. Without a clear temporal trigger tied to Consultant's delivery of confirmations, the City's obligation is effectively open-ended, undermining Columbia Capital Management's ability to manage trade execution and settlement with certainty.
suggestions.original_text: Custodian. Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1) the City shall instruct the Custodian to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes, in accordance with copies of confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Custodian. Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1), the City shall, within one (1) Business Day following receipt of written trade confirmations from Consultant, instruct the Custodian to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes, in accordance with such written trade confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted imposes no affirmative obligation on Consultant to disclose actual or potential conflicts of interest to Columbia Capital Management, leaving the City entirely dependent on Consultant's self-policing with no ability to make informed decisions or take protective action when competing loyalties arise. The bond-purchase restriction is framed as Consultant's internal "policy" rather than a binding contractual obligation, which undermines its enforceability against Columbia Capital Management's interests. Without a mandatory disclosure requirement and a defined consequence upon disclosure, Columbia Capital Management has no contractual basis to direct Consultant's conduct, demand remediation, or seek alternative arrangements when a conflict materializes.
suggestions.original_text: Potential Conflicts of Consultant. It is understood that Consultant will be acting in a similar capacity for other institutional clients, including other municipal governments in Kansas and that investments and reinvestments for the Accounts of the City may differ from those made or recommended with respect to the accounts and clients even though the investment objectives may be the same or similar; however, Consultant shall allocate investment opportunities among clients on a fair and equitable basis. In addition, Consultant serves as financial advisor to municipal governments within and beyond Kansas that issue bonds (an “Issuer Client”), including, in the case of Kansas issuers, bonds eligible for investment by the City. To prevent any appearances of favoring an issuer client over an investment client, or of favoring an investment client over an issuer client, it is the policy of Consultant to not purchase bonds of an Issuer Client issuing bonds in the primary market on behalf an investing client or to purchase callable bonds of an Issuer Client at any time on behalf of an investing client. This policy serves to protect both clients from potential conflicts but may limit investment opportunities for the City from time to time.

suggestions.reason: The clause permits the City to amend Schedule X — which controls who may give binding instructions to Columbia Capital Management regarding the Accounts — "at any time" with no minimum advance notice period, leaving Columbia Capital Management exposed to acting on instructions from individuals whose authority has already been unilaterally changed or revoked without adequate warning, with no opportunity to adjust its operational procedures. This creates material financial and operational risk for Columbia Capital Management, as it could be held responsible for following instructions from persons whose authority was subsequently revoked without prior notice. Additionally, "aggregate performance data of Consultant that does not identify the City" is insufficiently precise, since data that does not explicitly name the City may still be attributable to it, creating reputational and confidentiality exposure for Columbia Capital Management. The clause also contains an unfilled placeholder, "Schedule X," which must be completed before execution to establish the operative list of City-authorized individuals.
suggestions.original_text: Directions to Consultant. The names, titles and authorities of the individuals authorized to act on behalf of the City with respect to the Accounts and this Agreement are set forth in Schedule X to this Agreement, which is attached hereto and incorporated herein, and which may be amended in writing at any time by the City with notice provided to Consultant. Consultant may include information regarding the Accounts in aggregate performance data of Consultant that does not identify the City.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Directions to Consultant. The names, titles and authorities of the individuals authorized to act on behalf of the City with respect to the Accounts and this Agreement are set forth in Schedule X to this Agreement, which is attached hereto and incorporated herein, and which may be amended in writing by the City upon at least ten (10) days' prior written notice to Consultant. Consultant may include information regarding the Accounts in aggregate performance data of Consultant that does not identify, and cannot reasonably be attributed to, the City.

suggestions.reason: The Management Fees clause as drafted exposes Columbia Capital Management to material financial and operational risk by omitting four market-standard protections: no payment due date is specified, leaving Columbia Capital Management with no certainty as to when sums fall due; there is no right to dispute an invoice or mechanism to treat disputed amounts pending resolution, meaning Columbia Capital Management could be in default merely by withholding a contested charge; there is no constraint on Consultant unilaterally changing the fee rate, creating exposure to fee increases without Columbia Capital Management's consent; and the clause is silent on late-payment consequences, leaving that exposure entirely undefined and subject to Consultant's characterization. Without these protections, Columbia Capital Management faces unconstrained payment demands and no procedural recourse if invoices are disputed.
suggestions.original_text: Management Fees. Consultant will be compensated for its services under this Agreement in an amount equal to 0.20% of the market value of the Accounts, billed quarterly in arrears based upon the average of the month-end Account balances for such quarter, with a minimum fee for each quarter of $3,000. Market value, including accrued income, will be determinative for the purpose of calculating fees. Such amount shall be the sole compensation owing by reason of investment advisory services under this Agreement. The fee for services for any period less than a full quarterly period will be pro-rated on a daily basis on the annualized fee for the period and on the market value of the portfolio as described on the final date of such period.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Management Fees. Consultant will be compensated for its services under this Agreement in an amount equal to 0.20% of the market value of the Accounts, billed quarterly in arrears based upon the average of the month-end Account balances for such quarter, with a minimum fee for each quarter of $3,000. Consultant shall issue invoices within fifteen (15) days following the end of each calendar quarter, and undisputed amounts shall be due and payable by Columbia Capital Management within thirty (30) days of receipt of each invoice. Columbia Capital Management may dispute any invoice in writing within fifteen (15) days of receipt, and disputed amounts shall be withheld pending resolution without constituting a payment default. The fee rate set forth herein shall remain fixed for the term of this Agreement unless amended by written agreement signed by both parties. Market value, including accrued income, will be determinative for the purpose of calculating fees. Such amount shall be the sole compensation owing, inclusive of all expenses, by reason of investment advisory services under this Agreement. The fee for services for any period less than a full quarterly period will be pro-rated on a daily basis on the annualized fee for the period and on the market value of the portfolio as described on the final date of such period.

suggestions.reason: The term "Custodian" is undefined in the clause and, if not defined elsewhere in the Agreement, its meaning is open to dispute, which undermines the operative obligation on The City and indirectly weakens Columbia Capital Management's exculpation by leaving unclear who holds and votes the proxies. More significantly, the phrase "no responsibility in respect of the voting of proxies" is ambiguous in scope: a court could read it narrowly to mean only that Columbia Capital Management has no duty to cast votes, while still exposing Columbia Capital Management to claims for failing to provide proxy voting recommendations or analysis, or for losses flowing from The City's voting decisions. Adding "or liability of any kind" directly after "no responsibility" closes that interpretive gap and makes the exculpation enforceable on its face without altering The City's retained obligation.
suggestions.original_text: Proxy Voting. The City shall direct the Custodian in voting of all proxies and Consultant shall have no responsibility in respect of the voting of proxies.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Proxy Voting. The City shall direct the Custodian (as defined in the applicable custody agreement) in the voting of all proxies, and Consultant shall have no responsibility or liability of any kind in respect of the voting of proxies.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the representations Consultant makes to the City are limited to registration status and Form ADV delivery under the Investment Consultants Act of 1940, leaving Columbia Capital Management without any warranty that Consultant complies with all applicable laws governing performance of this Agreement or that the services and deliverables are free of third-party intellectual property claims — both material omissions that expose Columbia Capital Management to uncompensated regulatory and infringement risk. Additionally, the clause contains no remedy mechanism, so if any representation proves false, Columbia Capital Management has no express right to require re-performance or recover fees paid, forcing it to rely solely on a general breach claim. These gaps should be addressed in conjunction with the Agreement's indemnification and termination provisions to confirm that breach of these representations triggers those remedies as well.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant (i) is registered as an “investment adviser” under the Investment  Consultants Act of 1940 as amended (the “Consultants Act”); (ii) will promptly advise the City if at any time during the term of this Agreement Consultant ceases being so registered; and (iii) has delivered to the City a copy of Part II of its Form ADV or comparable Brochure pursuant to the Consultants Act;
suggestions.suggested_fix: Consultant (i) is registered as an "investment adviser" under the Investment Consultants Act of 1940 as amended (the "Consultants Act") and complies with all applicable laws and regulations governing the performance of this Agreement; (ii) will promptly advise the City if at any time during the term of this Agreement Consultant ceases being so registered; (iii) has delivered to the City a copy of Part II of its Form ADV or comparable Brochure pursuant to the Consultants Act; and (iv) warrants that the services provided hereunder do not infringe any third party's intellectual property rights. In the event of a breach of any representation or warranty in this Section, Consultant shall, at the City's election, re-perform the non-conforming services or refund the fees paid for such non-conforming services.

suggestions.reason: The fiduciary warranty as drafted contains no temporal limitation, meaning the Consultant could argue it applies only at the moment of execution rather than continuously throughout the engagement. For Columbia Capital Management, whose assets are being managed under this Agreement, this creates a material gap: if the Consultant's fiduciary status lapses or is challenged mid-engagement, Columbia Capital Management may have no contractual basis to enforce fiduciary duties for breaches occurring after signing. Anchoring the warranty to the Term of the Agreement is essential to preserve Columbia Capital Management's ability to hold the Consultant accountable on an ongoing basis for the duration of asset management activities.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant is a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement;
suggestions.suggested_fix: Consultant is, and shall remain throughout the Term of this Agreement, a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement;

suggestions.reason: The authority representation runs only in favour of Columbia Capital Management — the Consultant warrants its own authorization, but Columbia Capital Management makes no equivalent representation. This asymmetry exposes Columbia Capital Management to an enforceability challenge: a Consultant seeking to escape its obligations could argue that the Agreement lacks mutually established authority and that the arrangement is therefore not binding on Columbia Capital Management in any reciprocal sense. Market-standard professional services agreements require both parties to represent their authority to contract, and the absence of Columbia Capital Management's corresponding representation creates an unnecessary gap that could undermine the Agreement's integrity in a dispute.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant is duly authorized and fully empowered to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Each party is duly authorized and fully empowered to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement.
